output.summary: The 12-minute benchmark comes from chains with at least 60% pre-prepared or frozen components, and scratch kitchens were excluded, so it is not comparable to Copperleaf (E3). The 2024 trial cut ticket time by 1.9 minutes but dropped food quality and drew written complaints (E9). That makes the group's longer ticket time look like an accepted tradeoff, so the group-wide frozen-component switch and a 12-minute GM bonus target are risky. Riverside's slowdown plausibly traces to a missing sauté/pasta cook (E13). Marcus's reason for leaving is unestablished, and Kessler's blame rests on hearsay (E1), so replacing him is unjustified. Restoring Riverside's fourth line position and tracking it weekly is cheap and reversible. The evidence is thin, so many items stay unknown.
